sections.heading: Trip Overview
sections.content:
This comprehensive travel guide covers a relaxed 6-day family trip to Tokyo, Japan for 3 travelers. The focus is on shopping and experiencing Tokyo's famous food culture at a comfortable pace.

**Trip Details:**
• Travelers: 3 people (family)
• Origin: Bangkok, Thailand (BKK)
• Destination: Tokyo, Japan (NRT/HND)
• Dates: May 12-17, 2026 (5 nights)
• Accommodation: 2 rooms needed
• Trip Focus: Shopping & Food experiences
• Pace: Relaxed, not rushed

sections.heading: Flight Recommendations

rows: Budget option, nonstop, departs Don Mueang

sections.content: **Recommendation:** For a family trip focused on comfort, consider Thai Airways or ANA for daytime flights with full meal service. Budget travelers can save with Thai AirAsia X. Haneda Airport (HND) is closer to central Tokyo than Narita (NRT).

sections.heading: Hotel Recommendations
sections.content: **Recommendation:** MIMARU hotels are highly rated for families - spacious rooms with kitchenette facilities. Shibuya Excel Hotel Tokyu offers unbeatable location right above the famous Scramble Crossing. Book early as May is popular travel season.

sections.heading: Day 1 - Tuesday, May 12: Arrival Day
sections.content:
**Flight:** Depart Bangkok → Arrive Tokyo

**Afternoon/Evening:**
• Clear immigration and customs at Narita/Haneda
• Purchase Suica/Pasmo IC card at airport (¥2,000 each)
• Take Narita Express or Airport Limousine Bus to hotel
• Check into hotel, rest and freshen up

**Evening (Light Exploration):**
• Easy walk around hotel neighborhood
• Dinner at a local ramen shop or conveyor belt sushi
• Early night to recover from travel

**Recommended Dinner:**
• **Oreryu Shio Ramen** (Shibuya) - Try the butter corn ramen
• Or grab quick bites at the hotel area

**Tips:**
• Don't overplan - jet lag is real!
• Convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) have excellent ready-to-eat meals

sections.heading: Day 2 - Wednesday, May 13: Shibuya & Harajuku
sections.content:
**Morning (Sleep in, late breakfast):**
• Enjoy hotel breakfast or visit a local kissaten (coffee shop)
• Start exploring around 10-11 AM

**Late Morning - Afternoon: Shibuya District**
• 🛍️ **Shibuya 109** - Iconic fashion building, youth brands
• 📸 **Shibuya Scramble Crossing** - World's busiest intersection
• 🛍️ **MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya** - 24-hour discount store (7-10 min walk from Shibuya 109)
  - Tax-free shopping for tourists
  - Electronics, cosmetics, snacks, souvenirs
• 🍽️ **Lunch at Uobei Sushi** - Fun sushi train experience near Don Quijote

**Afternoon: Harajuku**
• 🚶 Walk from Shibuya to Harajuku (15 min) or take train
• 🛍️ **Takeshita Street** - Famous pedestrian shopping street
• 🍦 Try colorful crepes and sweets
• 🌳 **Meiji Shrine & Yoyogi Park** - Peaceful escape (optional)

**Evening Dinner:**
• **Hamaguri** (Shinjuku) - Shellfish specialty restaurant
• Fresh oysters, clam dishes, unique mollusk sashimi

**Free Time:** Evening stroll in Shinjuku

sections.heading: Day 3 - Thursday, May 14: Shinjuku Shopping Day
sections.content:
**Morning:**
• Leisurely breakfast
• Start around 10-11 AM

**All Day: Shinjuku Shopping Paradise**
• 🏬 **Isetan Department Store** - Luxury department store
  - Depachika (basement food hall) is amazing!
• 🏬 **Takashimaya Times Square** - Major shopping complex
• 🛍️ **Don Quijote Shinjuku Kabukicho** - 24-hour, multi-floor
• 🛍️ **Lumine EST** - Fashion mall connected to station
• 🎮 **Bic Camera** - Electronics haven

**Lunch:**
• **Teuchi** (Shinjuku) - Best soba noodles with tempura
  - Near Shinjuku Station, popular with locals
  - Go before 11:30 AM to avoid queues

**Afternoon:**
• Continue shopping or take a break at hotel
• 🌃 **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building** - Free observation deck (closes 10 PM)
  - Amazing sunset/night views!

**Dinner:**
• **Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane)** - Atmospheric alley with tiny yakitori bars
• Or try a nice izakaya in Shinjuku

**Evening:** Explore Kabukicho nightlife area (family-friendly areas exist)

sections.heading: Day 4 - Friday, May 15: Ginza Luxury & Tsukiji
sections.content:
**Morning: Tsukiji Outer Market**
• Start early (9-10 AM) for fresh seafood breakfast
• 🍣 Fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (egg omelet), seafood skewers
• Great for food lovers - walk and eat!

**Late Morning - Afternoon: Ginza District**
• 🏬 **Ginza Six** - Premium luxury mall
• 🛍️ **Uniqlo Ginza** - 12-floor flagship store
• 🛍️ **MUJI Ginza** - World's largest MUJI
• 🏬 **Mitsukoshi Department Store** - Classic luxury
• 🍫 **Don Quijote Ginza** - Wines and luxury goods

**Lunch:**
• Stay at Tsukiji for fresh sushi
• Or try a high-end lunch in Ginza (many affordable lunch sets)

**Afternoon Option:**
• 🎭 **Kabuki-za Theatre** - See the famous building (shows available)
• 🌸 Walk to **Hama-rikyu Gardens** (beautiful Japanese garden)

**Dinner:**
• **Tenmatsu Tempura** (Nihonbashi) - Famous for light, crispy tempura
  - Traditional tempura restaurant with set menus
• Or return to Shinjuku for dinner

sections.heading: Day 5 - Saturday, May 16: Asakusa & Last Shopping
sections.content:
**Morning: Asakusa Traditional District**
• 🛕 **Senso-ji Temple** - Tokyo's oldest temple
• 🛍️ **Nakamise Shopping Street** - Traditional souvenirs, snacks
  - Japanese crackers, fans, lucky charms
• 📸 Great photo opportunities!

**Late Morning:**
• 🛍️ **Don Quijote Asakusa** - Good for last-minute shopping
• Traditional Japanese items and modern goods

**Lunch:**
• **Unagi (Eel) Restaurant** in Asakusa - Traditional grilled eel
• Or try monjayaki in nearby Tsukishima

**Afternoon Options:**

**Option A - Tokyo Skytree Area:**
• 🗼 **Tokyo Skytree** - Tallest tower in Japan
• 🛍️ **Tokyo Solamachi** - Shopping mall at Skytree base

**Option B - Akihabara (if interested):**
• 🎮 Electronics and anime/manga paradise
• Great for unique Japanese pop culture items

**Option C - Relaxation:**
• Return to hotel, enjoy hotel amenities
• Pack and organize purchases

**Farewell Dinner:**
• **Nemuro Hanamaru** - Premium conveyor belt sushi from Hokkaido
  - Expect 1-2 hour wait, but worth it!
  - Much better quality than regular chain sushi
• Or splurge on a nice kaiseki or yakiniku meal

sections.heading: Day 6 - Sunday, May 17: Departure
sections.content:
**Morning:**
• Enjoy final hotel breakfast
• Last-minute packing
• Check out (store luggage if needed)

**If Time Allows (for Narita departures):**

**Option A - Shisui Premium Outlets (Near Narita):**
• Located between Tokyo and Narita Airport
• Coach, Kate Spade, Asics, Lacoste, and more
• Tax-free shopping available
• Take direct bus from Tokyo Station
• Plan 2-3 hours for shopping before heading to airport

**Option B - Airport Early:**
• Explore Narita Airport shopping
• Excellent duty-free shops
• Last chance for Japanese snacks and souvenirs

**Travel to Airport:**
• Narita Express: 1 hour from Tokyo/Shinjuku
• Airport Limousine Bus: 85-120 minutes
• Arrive at airport 3 hours before international flight

**Departure:** Fly back to Bangkok

**Don't Forget:**
• Tax refund at airport (if applicable)
• Use remaining IC card balance at airport shops
• Japanese souvenirs from duty-free

sections.heading: Must-Try Restaurants

rows: Best soba in Shinjuku, lunch only

sections.content:
**Food Tips:**
• Tabelog.com is the Japanese Yelp - use it to find top-rated restaurants
• Many restaurants have lunch sets (teishoku) that are much cheaper than dinner
• Look for restaurants with plastic food displays outside - helps with ordering
• "Oishii!" means delicious - use it often!

sections.heading: Shopping Guide
sections.content:
**Shopping Tips:**
• Bring your passport for tax-free shopping (purchases over ¥5,000 at single store)
• Don Quijote accepts coupons - download their app for extra discounts
• Department store basements (depachika) have amazing food to take away
• Many stores open at 10-11 AM - don't rush mornings

sections.heading: Outlet Mall Option
sections.content:
**Shisui Premium Outlets**
• Location: Between Tokyo and Narita Airport
• Getting There: Direct bus from Tokyo Station (1 hour)
• Brands: Coach, Kate Spade, Boss, Lacoste, Levi's, Asics, Theory, Nike
• Hours: 10AM-8PM
• Perfect for: Last day shopping before Narita departure

**Gotemba Premium Outlets** (Day Trip)
• Japan's largest outlet mall
• Views of Mt. Fuji on clear days
• 2-3 hours from Tokyo by bus
• Better for longer visits with dedicated day

**Recommendation:** Shisui is more practical for your itinerary - visit on departure day before heading to Narita Airport.

sections.heading: Practical Tips
sections.content:
**Transportation:**
• **Suica/Pasmo Card:** Buy at airport, load with ¥5,000-10,000. Works on all trains, buses, convenience stores
• **JR Pass:** NOT recommended for Tokyo-only trip (not cost-effective for 5 days in city)
• **Tokyo Metro:** Very efficient, runs until midnight
• **Walking:** Tokyo is very walkable - wear comfortable shoes!

**Money:**
• Japan is still cash-heavy - carry ¥30,000-50,000 per person
• 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards
• Credit cards accepted at major stores, less at small restaurants
• Tax-free shopping: Bring passport, spend ¥5,000+ at single store

**Communication:**
• Rent pocket WiFi or buy Japan SIM at airport
• Download Google Translate (with Japanese offline pack)
• Download Japan Transit app for train navigation

**Weather (May):**
• Average temperature: 15-23°C (59-73°F)
• Light jacket for evenings
• Umbrella recommended (spring showers possible)
• Comfortable for walking!

**Etiquette:**
• No tipping in Japan
• Don't eat while walking (except at food markets)
• Keep quiet on trains
• Remove shoes when entering some restaurants
• Bow slightly when greeting

sections.heading: Budget Estimate
sections.content: **Note:** Shopping budget varies greatly based on personal preferences. Set aside additional budget for souvenirs and purchases. May is shoulder season with good weather but not peak prices.

sections.heading: Packing Checklist
sections.content:
**Essential Documents:**
☐ Passport (valid 6+ months)
☐ Flight tickets/confirmations
☐ Hotel reservations
☐ Travel insurance documents
☐ Credit/debit cards
☐ Japanese Yen cash

**Electronics:**
☐ Phone + charger
☐ Power bank
☐ Camera
☐ Universal adapter (Japan uses Type A plugs, same as US)
☐ Pocket WiFi / SIM card (rent at airport)

**Clothing (May weather):**
☐ Light layers
☐ Comfortable walking shoes (VERY important!)
☐ Light jacket/cardigan for evenings
☐ Umbrella or rain jacket
☐ Casual dining outfits

**Other:**
☐ Medications
☐ Small daypack for shopping
☐ Foldable shopping bags (for purchases)
☐ Hand sanitizer
☐ Tissues/wet wipes

sections.heading: Useful Japanese Phrases
sections.content: **Tip:** Japanese people appreciate any effort to speak their language. Even a simple "Arigatou!" goes a long way!
